ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, S.O.R./2002-184; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46 (money laundering and terrorist financing offences); Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), S.B.C. 2002, c. 57 (BCBCA), Part 9.1 (transparency register of significant individuals, as added by S.B.C. 2019, c. 8); Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 21.1-21.4 (individual with significant control register; filing obligations introduced by the Budget Implementation Act, 2023). BCBCA s. 51.91 defines a significant individual by a 25% threshold of voting rights or fair-market value of shares. Accepting USDC as payment for data services does not, per se, make the entity a money services business (MSB) under the PCMLTFA; a formal reassessment is triggered if the entity begins exchanging, transferring, or custodially holding virtual currency.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access. The BC transparency register is filed with the Registrar of Companies and is accessible only to designated law-enforcement, tax, and regulatory authorities; it is not open to public search as of the preparation date. Federal CBCA transparency reforms contemplate phased public access for federal corporations only, and do not affect the BC provincial regime.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, 25%+ shareholders, and authorized signatories against: FINTRAC published indicators, the UN Consolidated Security Council List, the OFAC SDN List (for USD rails and US counterparties), EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists, and Canada's sanctions regulations under the Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17. Foreign and domestic politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members, and close associates require enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Cryptocurrency (USDC) inflows must be screened through commercial blockchain analytics to exclude sanctioned or high-risk wallet addresses, consistent with FINTRAC virtual-currency guidance. Negative hits must be escalated to the AML compliance officer within 24 hours; unresolved matches bar incorporation and financial-account onboarding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Online, operated by BC Registry Services, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia (https://www.corporateonline.gov.bc.ca); the NUANS name search report is integrated into the BC name-reservation workflow
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A BC corporate name must use Latin (Roman) alphabet letters, Arabic numerals, and permitted punctuation, together with a legal element in English or French (Ltd., Inc., Corp., Limitée, Incorporée, Corporation). Non-Latin script, including Chinese characters, may not serve as the registered legal name. A phonetically transliterated distinctive element is acceptable if legible in Roman characters; a separate Chinese-character trade name, if desired, must be protected through trademark registration and has no statutory effect as the corporate name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Trust, Loan, Insurance, Assurance - requires prior licensing by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) or the BC Financial Services Authority (BCFSA)
University, College, Institute - requires written consent of the BC Ministry of Post-Secondary Education and Future Skills
Engineer, Engineering, Professional Engineer - requires consent of Engineers and Geoscientists BC (EGBC)
Architect, Architectural - requires consent of the Architectural Institute of British Columbia (AIBC)
Accountant, Auditor, Law, Lawyer - requires consent of the applicable professional regulatory body
Canada, British Columbia, Vancouver, Victoria - restricted geographic indicators requiring a verifiable connection to the jurisdiction and a non-misleading use
Hospital, Private Hospital - restricted under the Hospital Act consent requirements
Corporation, Incorporated, Ltd., Inc. - permitted only as the legal element; prohibited as the descriptive element
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the registrar issues a refusal notice with a reason code. (1) Submit a corrected Name Reservation Request through BC Corporate Online using an amended distinctive or descriptive element. (2) If the refusal arises from a conflict or confusing similarity, obtain a signed letter of consent or disclaimer from the conflicting name holder and resubmit with that letter under BCBCA ss. 22-23. (3) If the refusal involves a restricted token, attach the required regulatory consent (e.g., EGBC, AIBC, or BCFSA letter) to the resubmission. (4) A formal written reconsideration may be addressed to the Registrar of Companies, BC Registry Services, PO Box 9431 Stn Prov Govt, Victoria, BC V8W 9V3, with supporting evidence and legal submissions; the Registrar renders a written decision within 30 days. (5) If the Registrar affirms the refusal, an application for judicial review may be filed in the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241, within 60 days of the final administrative decision. In the interim, the applicant may incorporate under a BC numbered company and later pass an ordinary or special resolution to change its name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible. The BCBCA requires a registered office and a records office at a physical street address within British Columbia at all times; a post-office box alone is insufficient. A commercial registered-agent suite or virtual office that maintains a real street address, accepts service of process, and provides document storage satisfies the statutory requirement for a license-exempt data-API business with no physical storefront. The registered office and records office must be disclosed in the Notice of Office Address at incorporation and updated within 30 days of any change.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low. Estimated probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 24 months is approximately 8% for a non-regulated, license-exempt data-API entity; the probability of a desk-based CRA records request (letter or digital) is approximately 20%. Unannounced visits increase materially if tax arrears arise, a PEP or OFAC flag is triggered, a FINTRAC suspicious-transaction report is filed, or the entity is later characterized as an MSB.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c 57 (BCBCA), ss 10–15, 17–20, 47–52; Companies Regulation B.C. Reg. 2005/5 as amended
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, BC Ministry of Finance (British Columbia Corporate Registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (with Notice of Articles) submitted under BCBCA s 10(1)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; a British Columbia company may incorporate with zero issued shares or one subscribed share; no mandatory escrow or capital deposit requirement. The incorporator must either subscribe for at least one share or the directors must set the terms of initial share issuance in accordance with BCBCA ss 10–11.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscribers to the Incorporation Application are appointed as first directors. RESOLVED that the registered office of the corporation be established at 555 Thurlow Street, Vancouver, BC, and that the Notice of Articles reflect this address. RESOLVED that the corporation issue and allot 100 Class A common shares to the founding subscribers for CAD 1.00 each, fully paid. RESOLVED that [full name] be appointed President, [full name] be appointed Secretary, and [full name] be appointed Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until successors are elected. RESOLVED that officers are authorized to open corporate bank accounts, engage accountants, and file all post-incorporation registrations as required by law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries Online (BC Corporate Online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search through BC Registries Online or an authorized service provider. Submit a name reservation request to the BC Registrar of Companies to secure a distinct corporate name. Ensure the proposed name does not conflict with existing trademarks, corporate names, or restricted words. Pay the name reservation fee and record the reservation number.
required_dossiers: Supporting justification for any exempt or special name component
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is refused, submit alternative names or file a reconsideration request with the BC Registrar within 14 days, providing evidence of distinctiveness or acquired user recognition.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Incorporation Application, Notice of Articles, and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries Online / Authorized Legal or Corporate Services Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Incorporation Application and draft the Notice of Articles, including the registered office address, directors' names and addresses, share structure, and authorized capital. Prepare Articles that conform to BCBCA requirements; either adopt the standard Articles or customize them with special rights and restrictions. Obtain each incorporator's and first director's signed consent to act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry identifies incomplete or inconsistent information, revise the affected forms and resubmit; technical or structural deficiencies in Articles can be cured by filing an Amendment under BCBCA s 88 after incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with the BC Registrar of Companies and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, BC Ministry of Finance (BC Corporate Registry), Victoria, BC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Electronically submit the completed Incorporation Application, Notice of Articles, Articles, and any required consents through BC Registries Online, or file by mail or in person at the Registry. Pay the prescribed filing fee. Upon approval, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation, which establishes legal corporate existence.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond within the registry's stated deadline with corrected documents or a written explanation; an erroneous rejection may be cured by administrative review or by re-incorporating under a new name reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Organizational Formalities and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation's Registered and Records Office; Directors of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Certificate of Incorporation, hold the first board meeting or execute unanimous written resolutions. Adopt bylaws or rely on the Articles; issue share certificates to subscribers; record share transfers in the securities register; establish the corporate minute book, seal, and records office. File any initial notice of change of directors or registered office if not already recorded.
required_dossiers: Minute book and corporate records binder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If discrepancies appear in the filed records, submit a Correction of Records application or an Amending Notice under BCBCA s 33 to reconcile the registry and corporate records; late filings are subject to late fees but may be cured with a reinstatement or correction request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); BC Ministry of Finance; WorkSafeBC; relevant municipal authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register with CRA to obtain a Business Number (BN), and account for Goods and Services Tax/Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST), Payroll Source Deductions, and, if applicable, Import/Export Account. Register for the BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) account and any municipal business licence in the municipality where the registered office operates. Workers' compensation clearance must be obtained from WorkSafeBC if the company has employees.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or BC Tax Authority queries the registration, provide supplemental verification of corporate identity or proof of office address; an administrative penalty may be waived if the correction is voluntarily disclosed under the CRA Voluntary Disclosure Program.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no physical industrial establishment. For office-based software/data services, the City of Vancouver business licence division and BC Ministry of Finance regulate commercial occupancy and tax registration, not industrial manufacturing licensing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required — no manufacturing or heavy industry permit for ISIC 6201 (computer programming/data processing) activities; an ordinary municipal business licence is the only operational permit if physical office premises are maintained.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not applicable — the BC Environmental Assessment Act does not apply to commercial data/API services. Where leased premises are occupied, landlord environmental compliance and local municipal waste bylaws govern.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no full EIA, registration, or permitting requirement for a purely digital service business with no effluent, no combustion, and no industrial discharge.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable in the absence of manufacturing operations. If office premises generate general municipal waste or e-waste, the facility must comply with local waste segregation standards and the BC Recycling Regulation for electronic equipment disposal; no wastewater or VOC thresholds are triggered for server and data processing activities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For any leased commercial office space, the municipal building department must confirm occupancy and fire safety clearance; WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety registration and clearance is required when employees are engaged. A fire safety inspection certificate from the local fire department is required before commencement of office operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); portal: My Business Account, https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html. British Columbia is a non-harmonized province: the federal GST is administered by the CRA, while the BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) is administered separately by the British Columbia Ministry of Finance, Consumer Taxation Branch, via eTaxBC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a federal or BC Business Corporation: (1) incorporate under the Canada Business Corporations Act or the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia); the CRA automatically issues the nine-digit Business Number (BN) upon receipt of corporate registry data via the OneStop/Corporations Canada integration. (2) Register program accounts using Business Registration Online or My Business Account: RC for corporation income tax, RT for GST/HST, and PD for payroll where applicable. (3) For a foreign entity without Canadian incorporation, file Form RC1Q (Request for a Business Number and Program Accounts) with the CRA non-resident business unit; the foreign entity may also be required to extra-provincially register under the BC Business Corporations Act if it carries on business in BC. (4) A GST/HST registration becomes effective on the date the entity ceases to be a small supplier, or on an earlier requested date where voluntary registration is elected.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: a Canadian business corporation is a resident taxpayer subject to federal corporate income tax (15%) and BC provincial corporate income tax (12%) on worldwide income; no pass-through eligibility, no territorial election, and no tax-exempt zone. The BC small business deduction reduces the combined rate to approximately 11% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income where eligibility conditions are met.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box election; corporate tax classification is fixed by incorporation law. Hybrid mismatch rules have been proposed/implemented through Income Tax Act sections 18.1-18.3 (draft legislation released November 2022), effective for taxation years beginning on or after October 1, 2023. Relevant statutory elections include: subsection 85(1) tax-deferred incorporation rollover; subsection 256 corporate attribution/amalgamation elections; GST/HST voluntary registration under subsection 240(3) of the Excise Tax Act; the quick method of accounting election; and section 156 associated-corporation loss-transfer elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act; British Columbia is not an HST province, so the GST rate is 5% and is imposed separately from the BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) of 7%. Digital/data-processing services and cloud software consumed in BC may also attract the separate 7% BC PST, which falls outside the CRA-administered GST regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies, including zero-rated export supplies, over any four consecutive calendar quarters; registration is required within 30 days of ceasing to be a small supplier, and voluntary registration is available below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None at the federal level. Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or transactional invoice certification for GST/HST purposes; the CRA accepts paper, PDF, and EDI/XML filings. A voluntary Pan-Canadian e-invoice standard based on Peppol BIS 3.0 is progressively being adopted for B2B and federal B2G procurement. CRA digital filing channels (GST/HST NETFILE and My Business Account APIs) relate to return submission, not per-invoice clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Schedule VI, Part V, section 9 of the Excise Tax Act zero-rates a service supplied to a non-resident recipient unless the service relates to real property situated in Canada, relates to tangible personal property situated in Canada, is rendered to a non-resident individual while present in Canada, or is a prescribed service under section 9.1 supplied for consumption in Canada. For the ISIC 6201 web-scraping and proxy API gateway, zero-rating applies where the recipient is a non-resident, is not registered under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act, and consumes the API/data output outside Canada; the supplier must document the non-resident status and overseas place of consumption. Goods exported from Canada are zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V, conditional on physical export in accordance with the Customs Act and prescribed evidence requirements. BC PST does not apply where the digital service is not acquired for use in BC.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration filed through the Canada Export Reporting System / CBSA CARM platform (B13A or CAED) for any goods; for pure API data services, a written service agreement with the non-resident recipient identifying the place of supply and place of consumption, together with the underlying commercial invoice
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill, or the digital equivalent (API access logs, server timestamps, IP geolocation records) evidencing delivery/performance outside Canada

Inward remittance certificate or equivalent foreign-currency receipt evidence (SWIFT MT103, Stripe payout ledger, or USDC on-chain transaction record) demonstrating receipt and repatriation of export proceeds within 180 days of supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA may reassess within four years (unlimited where misrepresentation, fraud, or failure to file exists), deny the zero-rating, assess 5% GST on the disputed supplies, and claw back related input tax credits. False statements made knowingly or through gross negligence attract a penalty of the greater of CAD 100 and 25% of the net tax under Excise Tax Act section 285.1; tax evasion prosecutions under section 341 can result in fines up to CAD 25,000 and imprisonment. Unremitted amounts bear compound interest, and directors may incur personal liability under section 323. Although Canada does not impose a statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline, exceeding the 180-day benchmark, without credible commercial justification, materially increases audit scrutiny of the underlying export documentation and may lead to retrospective assessment of GST plus penalties and interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada). Cross-border banking supervision is administered jointly with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), and Payments Canada (operator of the Lynx RTGS and ACSS clearing systems). In British Columbia, the BC Financial Services Authority (BCFSA) licenses money-services businesses and virtual-currency dealers under the Money Services Business Act. Canada maintains no exchange-control law: the Bank of Canada does not approve, license, or obtain declarations for individual cross-border payments, export proceeds, or profit remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is a fully convertible G10 currency with unrestricted current-account and capital-account convertibility under the Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act. The exchange rate is market-determined and floating; no surrender, repatriation, advance-deposit, or exchange-control approval obligations exist. For the target entity (a BC business corporation operating an ISIC 6201 public commercial web-scraping and proxy-API gateway), profit-remittance hurdles are fiscal rather than monetary: (1) Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (statutory 25%, treaty-reduced to 5%–15% for dividends, interest, and royalties) applies to distributions to foreign shareholders; (2) exported data and API services are zero-rated for GST/HST under ETA section 7, eliminating domestic indirect-tax friction; (3) the company must maintain Canadian economic substance to avoid CRA and OSFI-conduct audit challenge, but no central-bank permission is ever required. Non-resident ownership of 100% of the BC corporation is lawful; the Investment Canada Act applies only to reviewable acquisitions of control of existing Canadian businesses, not to de novo incorporation and initial capitalization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation requirement for export receipts or any foreign-currency earnings. A BC exporter of API-metadata, scraping data, or gateway services may retain 100% of USD or any third-currency proceeds indefinitely, either in Canadian accounts or abroad. The only compliance obligations are: (i) FINTRAC large-EFT and large-virtual-currency transaction reporting, which attaches to financial institutions and VASPs rather than to the exporter; (ii) CRS/FATCA due-diligence documentation; (iii) CRA recognition of foreign-exchange gains or losses under ITA section 39(1); and (iv) use of accurate wire purpose codes to allow the bank's own correspondent-bank compliance. No Bank of Canada export-proceeds declaration exists.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
Bank of Montreal (BMO, including BMO Harris Bank in the United States)
National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Medium, permissible only in a sponsored-bank model. Offshore fintech EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, Revolut Business) cannot hold a direct settlement account at Payments Canada and must operate through a Canadian schedule I bank sponsor. In British Columbia, the Money Services Business Act and FINTRAC MSB rules require registration/licensing where the entity carries on foreign-exchange, remittance, or virtual-currency payment business in the province. For the ISIC 6201 scraping-API enterprise, an EMI is acceptable for low-value operational disbursements and agent micro-payouts, but not for the statutory capital escrow, tax-relevant dividend remittance, or major trade settlements, which should remain on tier-1 Canadian bank rails. The dual-rail strategy adopted here is: tier-1 schedule I bank for CAD/USD fiat treasury, plus a FINTRAC-registered licensed VASP solely for USDC programmatic payouts, with documented treasury controls bridging the rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: De facto physical presence is required despite technical remote-verification legality. FINTRAC's PCMLTFA rules permit remote identification using independent, reliable source documents, a two-factor check, and Canadian notary verification; however, all OSFI-regulated schedule I banks internally classify newly incorporated BC companies with non-resident UBOs as high-risk and apply a 'no remote non-resident underwriting' override. The minimum acceptable board stack is: (a) at least one physical KYC interview in Canada (Vancouver or Toronto) for the lead director and all ultimate beneficial owners; (b) a physical, non-virtual BC registered office evidenced by a lease agreement; (c) original or certified notarial corporate records (notice of articles, registers of directors and shareholders, special resolutions); and (d) Canadian tax identifiers (CRA business number, corporate tax account) with a confirmed incorporation filing. Compliance strategy: schedule the board presentation at the chosen bank's commercial banking centre before account activation, and budget 4–8 weeks for enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO / offshore control structure — bank perceives a shell pattern: foreign individual(s) owning 100% of a newly incorporated BC corporation with no Canadian banking history, no local employees at inception, and a purely digital revenue model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified true copies of BC incorporation records under the Business Corporations Act (notice of articles, register of directors, register of shareholders, share allotment resolutions); certificate of good standing from the BC Registrar of Companies; CRA business number and T2 corporate tax filing plan (or confirmation-of-registration receipt); notarized passport copies plus a Canadian bank-acceptable identity-verification certificate for each UBO; source-of-wealth letter supported by brokerage statements or audited financial statements; registered-office lease and corporate-secretary engagement letter evidencing substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction-flow mismatch — web-scraping API generates high-frequency, geographically dispersed micro-invoicing (hundreds of Stripe receipts and USDC settlements) that is disproportionate to the declared revenue forecast and lacks physical inventory, triggering layering or trade-based money-laundering flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved rolling 12-month cash-flow forecast and annual treasury budget; master service agreements and reseller agreements with named enterprise clients; engineering-validated API usage telemetry (metered request logs) exportable to the bank's transaction-review portal; monthly aged-A/R reconciliation and invoice ledger; public product documentation evidencing the paid SaaS data-pipeline model; internal financial-controls matrix separating treasury, billing, and procurement signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cryptocurrency treasury (USDC) and payment aggregator (Stripe) exposure — banks categorize stablecoin-touching corporate accounts as high-risk for sanctions evasion, unhosted-wallet exposure, and unregulated payment intermediation; USDC redemption flows also create CRA-visible crypto-disposition events.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FINTRAC registration evidence or a Canadian legal opinion confirming the entity is not itself an MSB or VASP; treasury policy capping USDC holdings at 5% of operating liquidity and prohibiting unhosted-wallet counterparties; whitelisted corporate wallet addresses and Circle USDC reserve attestations; KYT/chain-analytics reports (Chainalysis or TRM) for every deposit and withdrawal; CPA agreed-upon-procedures report reconciling fiat wire entries with USDC mint/burn events; OFAC/UN sanctions screening and FINTRAC Travel-Rule compliance procedure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible-service tax ambiguity — high-margin data-delivery receipts with minimal physical footprint raise transfer-pricing, permanent-establishment, and sham-substance concerns under CRA audit policy and OSFI borrower-conduct reviews.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation prepared under OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines benchmarking third-party API-data licensing arrangements; intercompany agreements if a multinational group exists; evidence of Canadian operational substance (co-located compute hardware, employment contracts, BC payroll remittances, WorkSafeBC coverage); filed CRA T2/T106 returns and PST/GST returns; board minutes evidencing Canadian management decisions; ISO 27001 and SOC 2 attestations corroborating a real technology enterprise.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after the anniversary of the date of incorporation; government filing fee CAD 30.00 (approx. USD 22)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of CAD 50 per overdue year; failure to file annual reports for two consecutive years may result in administrative strike-off/dissolution by the Registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including financial statements and shareholder/ownership schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the taxation year-end, regardless of filing method; no government filing fee, but any tax balance must be paid by the deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance owing, plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months; repeat failure incurs 10% base penalty plus 2% per month; continued non-compliance may trigger prosecution.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A BC private business corporation is not required to appoint an independent auditor unless shareholders pass a resolution requiring an audit, the company is an offering or public company, or another statute (e.g., financial services licensing) imposes an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by the Canadian Accounting Standards Board, or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE - CPA Canada Handbook Part II) for eligible private BC corporations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the BC Business Corporations Act, a transparency register of significant individuals with 25% or more voting control must be maintained and kept current. Share transfers are recorded in the Register of Shareholders in the order received; the annual report certifies the registered office and current directors, and the transparency register must be available for inspection upon demand. No separate UBO annual return is filed with the BC Registrar.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of shareholder and director meetings
Articles, bylaws, resolutions, and corporate records

stage_6.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (CRA); filed electronically via CRA E-file / GSTNET? Actually: 'CRA Corporate Internet Filing (CIF)/ E-file through approved software'
stage_6.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal period); quarterly installment payments may apply
stage_6.statutory_deadline_rule: File within 6 months after fiscal year-end; balance-due day is 2 months after year-end (3 months for qualifying CCPCs), under ITA s. 150 and s. 157
